Dunleavy's action followed a New York Times report published Wednesday alleging that aides to Peltola and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee secretly recruited a retired teacher, Dan J. Sullivan, to run as a spoiler candidate.

Last week, the Justice Department filed a lawsuit seeking to block election certification if the incumbent senator loses due to 'voter confusion,' despite the Alaska Supreme Court previously allowing Dan J. Sullivan to appear on the ballot.

President Donald Trump called for Peltola's prosecution Wednesday, branding the alleged plot "voter fraud at the highest level," while Peltola dismissed the report as a "distraction" from Sen. Dan Sullivan's policy record.

The controversy underscores high stakes in Alaska's Senate race, as political analysts view the contest as critical in determining which party controls the chamber, prompting intensified scrutiny of unconventional campaign tactics.

California attorneys called the government's allegations "vague" and "not reliable," while First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli argued the state cannot "do nothing" when made aware of potential noncitizens on voter rolls.

title: Judge rejects US Justice Dept bid to block votes from alleged noncitizens in California

The Royal Spanish Football Federation suspended all 24 Copa del Rey matches scheduled for Wednesday as a "mark of respect," while rail operator ADIF halted traffic on the Madrid-Andalusia corridor indefinitely.

title: At least 68 people dead in Spain's second major train crash this year

summary: In the largest security breach in cryptocurrency history, hackers drained an estimated $6.3 billion from Binance hot wallets across 10 blockchains in a coordinated attack lasting roughly 20 minutes on Thursday evening.

Initial investigations indicate the breach originated from a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, enabling the attackers to gain access to a service container, utilize Ethereum's EIP-7702 feature to authorize malicious contracts, and execute unauthorized withdrawals without compromising wallet private keys.

Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attributed the massive intrusion to "TraderTraitor," an elite North Korean state-sponsored cyber warfare unit, noting that stolen assets were rapidly swapped into Ether and mixed with funds from previous exploits.

Binance immediately suspended all deposits and withdrawals, while coordinated intervention by the exchange, stablecoin issuers, and law enforcement successfully froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen assets on-chain.

Binance stated it will fully cover all unrecovered user losses through its SAFU reserve and corporate funds, while the broader crypto market suffered sharp declines—wiping out $170 billion in market capitalization and triggering over $1.3 billion in leveraged liquidations within 12 hours.
title: Binance says $6.3 billion stolen in biggest crypto heist in history

Pope Leo remains a registered voter at a New Lenox, Illinois, address despite leading 1.4 billion members of the Catholic Church from Vatican City. He did not renounce his U.S. citizenship upon becoming pope.

Public records show the pontiff voted in general elections from 2012 to 2024, utilizing The Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act, or UOCAVA, which allows U.S. citizens abroad to vote by mail.
Officials have not yet received Leo's completed ballot following his recent lung cancer surgery. He has previously clashed with President Donald Trump over foreign policy and immigration enforcement.
If Leo casts his ballot before the November 3 deadline, he will become the first pope to vote in a U.S. election while serving as head of the Church, a historic first.
title: Pope Leo Requests Illinois Mail Ballot for Midterm Elections

title: US promises tariff relief in talks with Audi on Georgia plant: Reuters

Five individuals have been charged so far, with more arrests expected; authorities also charged four defendants in New Jersey in connection with an alleged scheme involving more than $1.3 million in proceeds.

The FBI now has 45 open investigations across 26 field offices involving more than 20 U.S. attorneys' offices, while scammers funneled remaining funds into bank accounts with some money sent overseas to Kenya.
title: DOJ charges five in alleged $1.3 million student aid fraud scheme

title: New York state police to take over sexual assault complaints at Cornell University

summary: On Thursday, researchers published a study in Science characterizing Teghaza 001, a meteorite discovered in Mali that provides a rare snapshot of Mars' ancient crust and evidence of early water.

Lead author Yang Liu of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory called the meteorite 'a witness to a time when Mars was likely warmer and wetter,' offering critical clues about the planet's habitability and ancient environmental history.

Discovered in eight pieces, the nearly 800-gram rock differs from the 2.1 billion-year-old 'Black Beauty,' with unique igneous minerals indicating water percolated into the crust as it cooled and crystallized.

Multiple lines of evidence in Teghaza 001 show hydrogen and oxygen isotopes confirm water percolated into Mars' deeper crust, bolstering the notion that primordial Mars may have been conducive to microbial life.
Study co-author Lee Saper of NASA's Ames Research Center said the rock complements satellite data, revealing how early Mars' evolution diverged from Earth's when life was beginning on our planet.
title: Martian Meteorite Found in the Sahara Is 4.1 Billion Years Old

Theresa Aretino, Cynthia Fernandez, and Betty Larkin pursued claims of design defect, fraud, and negligence, alleging the weedkiller caused their non-Hodgkin lymphoma diagnoses.
Bayer is seeking a $7.25 billion settlement regarding approximately 65,000 other pending Roundup cases while defending the product's safety worldwide.

Despite the International Agency for Research on Cancer labeling glyphosate "probably carcinogenic" in 2015, Bayer rejects the study, citing the Environmental Protection Agency's consistent approval of Roundup as safe.
title: Bayer wins Roundup weedkiller cancer trial while awaiting settlement ruling

The agency intends to ban Chinese labs from testing United States electronics by December 2028, and California-based Digitalsystem Technology was recently added to a national security risk list due to Chinese ownership links.
title: US plans to ban Chinese telecom firms from direct access to US phone numbers

title: Reddit puts logged in experience first as Google AI hits traffic

summary: Two helicopters collided midair on Thursday, October 29, near McMinnville Municipal Airport in Oregon, approximately 35 miles southwest of Portland, prompting an emergency response.
The Federal Aviation Administration identified the aircraft as a Robinson R22 carrying one pilot and an Airbus H125 carrying two people, bringing the total number of occupants to three.

Authorities closed Highway 233 near Dayton and nearby local roads following the collision, while police, firefighters and medical personnel responded to the scene; officials urged the public to avoid the area.
Three people aboard two helicopters died after the aircraft collided midair near an airport in northwest Oregon on Thursday afternoon, according to the Yamhill County sheriff.
title: 3 dead after 2 helicopters collide midair near Oregon airport, sheriff says

summary: On Thursday, the American Civil Liberties Union filed a class-action lawsuit challenging "inhumane and unconstitutionally punitive" treatment of detainees at the Miami Correctional Facility in Bunker Hill, Indiana.

The Trump administration converted the maximum-security prison into an immigration detention facility last year, expanding detention space by 1,000 beds with federal funds as part of an agreement with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement .

Plaintiffs allege "indiscriminate" use of solitary confinement, "rampant" excessive force, and "dangerously inadequate" medical care, with two deaths occurring at the facility this year. The 72-page complaint details conditions including prolonged lockdowns and racial slurs.

"People are suffering, people have died, and more people will suffer and die if those continue," said Kathleen Hickey, a staff attorney at the ACLU of Illinois. Hickey called the state-federal partnership a source of crisis.

The partnership faces increasing scrutiny after at least 37 people died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody this fiscal year, the most in the agency's history according to the Migration Policy Institute.
title: Indiana ICE facility detainees spend weeks in solitary and face ‘medical crisis,’ lawsuit says

summary: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed will campaign Sunday in Detroit with Rep. Haley Stevens and South Carolina Rep. Jim Clyburn for a get-out-the-vote event at a church.
Their first joint appearance since the primary follows weeks of internal friction over El-Sayed's past remarks on Israel and an independent ad campaign linking support for Israel to grocery prices.

With the election approaching, Republican Mike Rogers appeared Wednesday with Republican Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas at an event hosted by the Republican Jewish Coalition in Birmingham, Michigan.
title: El-Sayed and Stevens to make rare joint appearance as Democrats seek unity in Michigan Senate race

summary: On Thursday, 19 U.S. lawmakers led by Rep. Mark Pocan, D-Wis., urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio not to support Colombia's plan for aerial coca spraying, warning the practice threatens human health and fragile Amazon rainforest ecosystems.

President Abelardo de la Espriella's government proposed a pilot project to spray up to 1,000 hectares of coca in Putumayo using glufosinate ammonium, an herbicide that lost approval for use in the European Union in 2018.
The lawmakers requested that Rubio clarify by Nov. 13 whether Washington pressured Colombia to restart the program and what safeguards exist for local communities and the environment.

Colombian Sen. Sandra Chindoy described the region as "not a spraying laboratory," while a Putumayo court previously halted the pilot after finding the government failed to meet strict legal requirements.

With coca cultivation reaching a record 261,000 hectares in 2024, lawmakers criticized President Donald Trump's administration for dismantling USAID programs that previously funded sustainable agriculture and ecotourism alternatives in the Amazon.
title: US lawmakers urge Trump administration to oppose Colombia’s Amazon aerial spraying plans

summary: Iran is importing billions in military supplies through a hidden network of more than 5,000 agencies, allowing its armed forces to maintain operations despite U.S. sanctions and an ongoing naval blockade.

Agencies operate under names beginning with MOD, referring to Iran's Ministry of Defense; one agency, MOD 346428, imported $2.3 billion in goods over an 18-month period examined by Reuters and 240 Analytics.

Supplies entered via cargo ships across the Caspian Sea from Russia, trucks from Central Asia , and freight aircraft from China; purchases included 435 trucks, machinery, electronics, and rocket fuel materials.

Records show purchases recovered to $77 million by May after dipping during the war's start, while the U.S. Treasury Department defended its sanctions as effective in severing Iran's economic lifelines.

Washington claimed it has severed Iran's economic lifelines despite the investigation revealing a sophisticated network bypassing restrictions through overseas intermediaries and multiple supply routes.
title: Iran's hidden web of military agencies is slipping hardware past the US blockade

summary: On Thursday, Chief Judge James Boasberg ordered the Trump administration to identify all states where it pressured officials to prevent non-U.S. citizens from voting, with disclosure due by Friday.
Democratic Party leaders sued on Oct. 20 to prevent election interference, with lawyer Uzoma Nkwonta calling the efforts an "unprecedented campaign" to interfere with state election duties.
A federal judge on Wednesday sided with California, blocking the Justice Department from excluding voters identified as "likely" noncitizens; the administration immediately appealed the ruling.
Boasberg intends to rule by Monday, the eve of Election Day, though he noted the administration could "moot this process at any time" by ending the challenged conduct.
Evidence from the states and Justice Department investigations shows non-citizen voting is extremely rare, while the administration maintains that plaintiffs' claims are overly broad and vague.
title: Judge presses the Trump administration for details on its campaign to stop noncitizens from voting

summary: On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Justice Department submitted a superseding complaint against former FBI officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, adding an obstruction charge before their scheduled preliminary hearing.
FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the Kansas City Field Office to investigate the agents following President Donald Trump's July 2020 address on foreign election interference.
Testifying Tuesday, FBI Special Agent Bryan Witt said he feared the probe would appear "political," and agreed that receiving a direct director tasking was "unusual" in his career.
Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui criticized prosecutors for filing the charge without judicial approval, stating the conduct bolstered defense claims the case is "atypical and bizarre."
Defense attorneys for Floris and Benavides allege the Trump administration weaponized the Justice Department for political gain, while prosecutors deny the case is politically motivated.
title: Ex-FBI officials accused of false statements about Hunter Biden press for dismissal of charges

summary: On Wednesday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed Arizona 's first New World screwworm case in a dog in Cochise County, marking the parasite's spread into a third U.S. state.
Since June, 71 cases have been reported across the United States, with 18 currently active; the parasitic fly advanced north from South America through Texas and New Mexico before reaching Arizona.

Federal and state officials are responding by establishing a 20-kilometer infested zone around the detection site, while the Arizona Department of Agriculture and USDA increase surveillance and release sterile flies to suppress the population.

State Veterinarian Dr. Ryan Wolker said, "We have been preparing for this possibility for a long while and are acting swiftly," as officials urge pet owners to check animals daily for wounds or maggots.
Plans for a Sterile Fly Dispersal Facility in Douglas, Arizona, continue to move forward as the USDA recently resumed livestock imports from Mexico at three ports of entry in Arizona and New Mexico.
title: New World Screwworm Confirmed in Arizona Dog, USDA Says

Sunday's report by N12 of a clash between Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir over a proposed military operation prompted the demand, raising concerns about potential miscalculations with Iran just two days before Israel's October 27 election.

Channel 12 reported that Zamir resisted the action, seeking signed legal authorization from Netanyahu, while military sources expressed concern that political leadership sought to "utilize the Iranian issue for political benefit."

Netanyahu dismissed the allegations as "nonsense" in a Channel 14 interview, while Prime Ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot criticized the reported "clash" and warned against treating national security as a "political bargaining chip."

Voters head to the polls on Tuesday with final surveys showing a slim lead for Eisenkot's coalition, as critics warn against risking IDF soldiers for political survival while no party appears positioned to form a government.
title: Former Israeli Defense Minister Seeks Treason Probe of Netanyahu

summary: On Monday, the Crown withdrew all criminal charges against 44 pro-Palestinian protesters arrested during an April 2024 sit-in at a downtown Montreal Scotiabank, officially ending the prosecution.
Protesters occupied the branch demanding Scotiabank divest from Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems, a move the bank eventually completed, which activists welcomed as a victory.

While 14 individuals previously pleaded guilty to municipal noise bylaw violations and paid $300 fines, defense lawyer Barbara Bedont noted most other protesters resolved their cases through community service.
Defendants challenged the charges under the Charter, arguing police violated their rights, and filed a formal complaint against the presiding judge alleging bias and unfair treatment.
Defense counsel Bedont warned that criminalizing peaceful sit-ins threatens the right to protest, suggesting the group's legal strategy likely influenced the Crown's decision to drop charges.
title: No Criminal Charges for Montreal Protesters Arrested at Bank Sit-In

Norway significantly outperforms the United States in metrics including life expectancy and GDP per capita of $106,000, while its sovereign wealth fund posted a record $184.3 billion profit.
